coverage.value: womenyouthapostles.org — NO per-person surface. The site is a small WordPress install with topical section pages (/who-we-are/*, /community-life/*, /apostolic-life/) and blog categories (/category/community-news/, /category/spiritual-life/, /category/community-house/, /category/ministry-events/, /tag/community-life/). Every blog post is filed under a single site-wide author, /author/womenyouthapostles/ — there are no per-member author pages. The Youth Apostles flat root-slug shape (youthapostles.org/tylerfabian) was tested and does NOT exist here; no /firstlast page surfaced on any query. No donate, give or support page surfaced either, so there is no per-person giving URL to mine. The only named-person surfaces on the whole domain are two directory pages: /who-we-are/our-general-council/ and /community-life/local-communities/. The community states it has 23 members and that they serve 'as volunteers and staff', so most of the roster is both unnamed publicly and of unknown support status. Verdict: not a mineable per-person target; harvestable ceiling is the ~7 named leaders on those two pages.

Bare site: queries on youthapostles.org were repeatedly hijacked by Wikipedia when the query carried a saint's or school's name (the St. Anthony / St. Leo parish sweep returned seven Wikipedia church articles and zero youthapostles.org results). Switching from the site: operator to allowed_domains=youthapostles.org fixed this completely and is the single most useful tactic found this run — every allowed_domains query returned ten on-domain results. Recommend the next wave use allowed_domains, not site:, for this target.

The -surname exclusion sweep degraded exactly as the brief predicted: the engine dropped the operators and re-served Fabian, Mee, Harbour, Frommelt and Zaso. That, plus the last two queries returning no new names, is the stop signal — the school/parish axis on youthapostles.org appears exhausted at the six person-pages found. The site's own /missionaries index page almost certainly lists more, but it cannot be paginated from search snippets.

https://www.youthapostles.org/ourcouncil — named hub; yielded John More and Fr. Jack Peterson. Snippet said other council members' names were not listed in the returned text.

needs_review.issue: Women Youth Apostles roster is 23 members but only ~7 are published
needs_review.finding: The community states it has 23 members; the website names only the five General Council members and three local directors (two of whom are also council members). The remaining members are not published anywhere on the domain.
needs_review.evidence: https://womenyouthapostles.org/who-we-are/our-general-council/ and https://womenyouthapostles.org/community-life/local-communities/; membership count from the community's own description.
needs_review.recommendation: Treat the domain as closed for enumeration. Do not spend further search budget on womenyouthapostles.org — there is no per-person surface and no giving surface to mine.

needs_review.issue: Tier for the entire Women Youth Apostles set is genuinely unresolved
needs_review.finding: WYA members are described by the community as serving 'as volunteers and staff' in youth and campus ministry. There is no donate page, no support page and no personal giving ask anywhere on womenyouthapostles.org. All seven WYA records were therefore graded Tier B rather than A.
needs_review.evidence: womenyouthapostles.org/apostolic-life/ and the site's own membership description; no give/donate/support URL surfaced in two targeted queries.
needs_review.recommendation: Before any outreach, establish whether WYA members raise personal support or are volunteers with outside income. If they are volunteers they are not an ICP fit at all and these seven should be reviewed out rather than re-tiered. Same screening logic the brief applies to Ratio Christi tent-makers.

needs_review.issue: General Council listing is dated 2023-2025 and may be stale
needs_review.finding: The Women Youth Apostles council page is labelled for the 2023-2025 term. As of the current date that term has lapsed, so Tiffany Lambert, Krysti Patient, Elena Adinaro, Makayla Puzio and MariTere Adinaro may no longer hold the roles recorded.
needs_review.recommendation: Verify roles before use. The people are real and current members; only the titles are at risk.

needs_review.issue: Fr. Jack Peterson's recorded role conflicts with a news report
needs_review.finding: The Youth Apostles /ourcouncil page names Fr. Jack Peterson as YA Consecrated Cleric Assistant Director, but the Arlington Catholic Herald published an article titled 'Fr. Peterson steps down as director of Youth Apostles'.
needs_review.recommendation: Verify current role. He is clearly a real, living member of the community; the discrepancy is between 'general director' (stepped down from) and 'consecrated cleric assistant director' (current), which may simply be two different posts.

needs_review.recommendation: Not emitted — a vacant or unnamed role is not a person. Re-probe /officestaff directly if page fetching becomes available.
